examples.question_text:
A student wrote $\frac{5x}{2} - \frac{x-3}{5} = \frac{25x-2(x-3)}{10} = \frac{25x-2x-6}{10} = \frac{23x-6}{10}$.
Describe the mistake and give the correct answer.
examples.solution_text:
The mistake is in expanding $-2(x-3)$: it equals $-2x+6$, because $-2$ multiplies each term.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{5x}{2}-\frac{x-3}{5}\\&=\frac{25x}{10}-\frac{2(x-3)}{10}\\&=\frac{25x-2(x-3)}{10}\\&=\frac{25x-2x+6}{10}\\&=\frac{23x+6}{10}\end{aligned}$
